cultural.vision_reason: This is a New Kingdom Egyptian talatat block carved in raised relief with the profile of Nefertiti and hieroglyphic text, from the Aten temple at Karnak — genuine Egyptian court art matching the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: Talatat: Nefertiti Offers to the Aten
physical.summary: The son of Amenhotep III, Akenaten, brought about the short-lived "monotheistic" revolution in Egyptian religion near the end of Dynasty 18. The young king constructed a temple complex to the Aten, the Sun Disk, at Karnak—where this relief originated—before he moved his capital to El Amarna. For reasons unknown, the figure of the Queen Nefertiti appears in these reliefs far more often than that of the king. Ironically, the Aten temples were dismantled to be used as foundations and fill for adaptations to the Great Temple of Amun, whom the Aten had briefly displaced.

location.made_in_place: Egypt, Karnak, New Kingdom (1540–1069 BCE), Dynasty 18, reign of Akhenaten (1351–1334 BCE)
